title: Runtime-aware rescorer scheduler and quality gates for multilingual rerank upgrades
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Introduce a runtime-aware scheduling layer and per-locale quality gating to safely upgrade cross-encoder rerank models across languages while meeting tail latency SLOs. The scheduler will pick rescorer variants at request time based on latency budget, locale, and recent regression signals; quality gates enforce rollback/canary limits when automated regression checks fail.
background: We currently run a single cross-encoder reranker family for most locales. Planned upgrades to newer cross-encoder variants (smaller quantized variants and larger high-quality variants) have produced occasional localized quality regressions and P99 latency spikes in peak traffic. Existing rollout tooling lacks per-locale gating and runtime selection that can route requests to a lower-latency fallback when SLOs are at risk. This ticket designs and implements a scheduler that balances quality and latency and a gating system tied to our regression harness and observability signals.
goals: Add a lightweight runtime scheduler that selects rescorer variant per request according to latency budget, locale, and customer tier
Implement per-locale quality gates driven by automated regression checks and traffic-weighted canaries
Provide safe fallback policies (quantized smaller variant or bi-encoder hybrid) when latency SLO or regression thresholds are breached
Expose metrics and traces for variant selection decisions and gate state in Console dashboards
success_metrics: No more than 3% increase in mean end-to-end rerank latency after rollouts (measured per-locale)
Canary regression detection catches precision-at-10 drops >= 2% within 1 hour of rollout
Automatic rollback triggers correctly route 100% of canary traffic to fallback within 2 minutes of breach
Per-locale upgrade rate reaches 80% coverage across supported locales without manual intervention
design_decisions: Scheduler lives in the rerank-ingress layer (sidecar adjacent to the API worker) to minimize added network hops
Decision inputs: latency budget (derived from customer tier and route), locale header, recent regression flags (from regression-service), current runtime SLAs, and model cost profile

Use a prioritized variant list per-locale: [preferred-high-quality, quantized-medium, low-latency-fallback, bi-encoder-fallback]. Scheduler attempts preferred variant and falls back based on measured queueing/exec latency
Quality gate evaluation uses the regression harness results (precision/recall by locale), real-time evaluation from a rolling sample, and anomaly detector on token-level scores
Canary rollout uses traffic-sliced cohorts: locale-aware 1% -> 5% -> 20% phased increase with automatic hold/rollback criteria
Rollout config stored in config-service with fast propagation; gate state persisted and emitted as events for tracing
implementation_steps: (Q1) Add selection API in rerank-ingress to accept decision context and return chosen model variant
(Q1) Extend model_catalog to include per-variant cost and latency profiles and locale compatibility metadata
(Q1) Integrate regression-service endpoint to fetch per-locale regression signals and gate status
(Q1) Implement fallback policies and immediate routing to bi-encoder scorer when latency budget violated
(Q1) Instrument metrics: variant_chosen{locale,variant}, variant_latency_ms, gate_state{locale,gate}, canary_failures
(Q1) Add console widgets for gate states and per-variant latency distributions
(Q2) Run internal canary against staging traffic with synthetic multilingual trace sets and the regression harness
(Q2) Gradual production rollout with automatic canary monitor jobs and rollback automation
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Integration tests in CI with mocked regression-service (no traffic)
Phase 1: Staging canary - route 5% of staging traffic (all locales) for 48h, run regression harness every 2h
Phase 2: Beta customers - select 3 customers across EU/NA/APAC, 1% traffic per customer for 24h
Phase 3: Per-locale progressive rollout 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% with automated hold if gate triggers
Emergency rollback: global gate flips will route all traffic to configured fallback variant within 2 minutes via control-plane event
regression_plan: Use existing rerank-eval-harness to sample candidate pools and compute precision@k and nDCG per-locale hourly
Define regression thresholds: precision@10 drop >= 2% OR nDCG drop >= 1.5% triggers canary hold
Implement real-time statistical test (bootstrap A/B) against baseline for canary slices
Post-mortem playbook: when gate activates, collect candidate-level diffs, model logits distributions, and recent token-level latencies
If regression is localized, mark locale blocked and notify PM/ML for triage
testing: Unit tests for scheduler decision logic (budget, locale, gate overrides)
Load tests simulating peak traffic with intentional latency noise to validate fallback behavior
Regression harness runs on every canary step; synthetic datasets for low-resource languages included
Chaos test: introduce artificial slowdowns in high-quality variant and assert 100% fallback within SLA window
End-to-end smoke with Console dashboards verifying gate transitions and metrics emission
open_risks: Risk: latency measurement lag could cause the scheduler to underrate available capacity and send too many requests to lower-quality variants
Risk: localized regressions may be noisy in low-volume locales - guard thresholds must account for sample size
Risk: added decision hop increases complexity and could introduce a new failure surface; mitigation: healthcheck + fast-path caching
Risk: misconfigured fallback could amplify cost by routing to more expensive variants; mitigation: include cost budget in decision inputs
